title_en: Exit and Entry Administration Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of regulating exit and entry administration, safeguarding the sovereignty, security and social order of the People's Republic of China, and promoting foreign exchanges and opening up.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to the administration of exit and entry of Chinese citizens, entry and exit of foreigners, and stay and residence of foreigners within the territory of China, as well as the border inspection of means of transport exiting and entering the country.

Article 3 The State shall protect the lawful rights and interests of Chinese citizens in exiting and entering the country.
The lawful rights and interests of foreigners within the territory of China shall be protected by law. Foreigners within the territory of China shall abide by Chinese laws and shall not endanger China's national security, harm social public interests, or disrupt social public order.

Article 4 The Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall, within the scope of their respective functions, be responsible for the administration of exit and entry affairs.
The embassies and consulates of the People's Republic of China abroad or other overseas institutions entrusted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (hereinafter referred to as visa-issuing authorities abroad) shall be responsible for issuing entry visas to foreigners outside the country. The exit and entry border inspection authorities shall be responsible for conducting exit and entry border inspections. The public security organs of local people's governments at or above the county level and their exit and entry administration agencies shall be responsible for the administration of the stay and residence of foreigners.
The Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs may, within the scope of their respective functions, entrust the exit and entry administration agencies of the public security organs of local people's governments at or above the county level or the foreign affairs departments of local people's governments at or above the county level with the acceptance of applications by foreigners for entry, stay and residence.
The Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall strengthen communication and coordination in the administration of exit and entry affairs, and shall closely cooperate with the relevant departments of the State Council, exercise their functions and powers according to law and assume responsibility in accordance with the division of respective functions.
Article 5 The State shall establish a unified information platform for exit and entry administration to achieve information sharing among relevant administrative authorities.

Article 6 The State shall establish exit and entry border inspection authorities at the ports open to foreign countries.
Chinese citizens, foreigners and means of transport shall exit or enter the country through the ports open to foreign countries. Under special circumstances, they may exit or enter the country at the places approved by the State Council or the departments authorized by the State Council. Persons and means of transport exiting or entering the country shall be subject to exit and entry border inspection.
The exit and entry border inspection authorities shall be responsible for the administration of the restricted zones at ports. As needed for maintaining national security and the order of exit and entry administration, the exit and entry border inspection authorities may conduct border inspections of the articles carried by persons exiting or entering the country. When necessary, the exit and entry border inspection authorities may conduct border inspections of the goods carried by means of transport exiting or entering the country, provided that the customs shall be notified.

Article 7 Upon approval by the State Council, the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs may, as needed for exit and entry administration, make provisions on the retention of biometric identification information such as fingerprints of persons exiting or entering the country.
Where a foreign government has special provisions on the issuance of visas to Chinese citizens or on exit and entry administration, the Chinese government may, depending on the circumstances, take corresponding reciprocal measures.

Article 8 The departments and institutions performing the duties of exit and entry administration shall take effective measures to continuously improve the level of service and administration, enforce the law impartially, provide convenience and efficiency, and maintain a safe and convenient exit and entry order.

Article 9 Chinese citizens shall apply for passports or other travel documents according to law when exiting or entering the country.
Chinese citizens going to other countries or regions shall also obtain visas or other entry permits of the destination country, unless the Chinese government has concluded visa exemption agreements with the government of another country or the Ministry of Public Security or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has otherwise provided.
Chinese citizens who exit or enter the country as seamen or work on foreign vessels shall apply for seamen's certificates according to law.

Article 10 Chinese citizens traveling between the mainland and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macao Special Administrative Region, and Chinese citizens traveling between the mainland and the Taiwan region shall apply for travel permits according to law and comply with the relevant provisions of this Law. The specific administrative measures shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 11 Chinese citizens exiting or entering the country shall submit their passports or other travel documents, or other exit and entry documents to the exit and entry border inspection authorities for inspection, complete the prescribed formalities, and may exit or enter the country only after being examined and permitted.
At ports where conditions permit, the exit and entry border inspection authorities shall provide special lanes and other facilitation measures for Chinese citizens exiting or entering the country.

Article 13 Chinese citizens residing abroad who wish to return to China for permanent residence shall, before entering the country, submit an application to the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China abroad or other overseas institutions entrusted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or may, in person or through domestic relatives, submit an application to the overseas Chinese affairs department of the local people's government at or above the county level of the intended place of residence.

Article 14 Where Chinese citizens residing abroad need to provide identity certificates for handling financial, education, medical, transportation, telecommunications, social insurance, property registration and other affairs within the territory of China, they may use their passports to prove their identity.

Article 50 When a means of transport exiting or entering the country leaves or arrives at a port, it shall undergo border inspection. The entry border inspection of means of transport shall be conducted at the port of first arrival, and the exit border inspection of means of transport shall be conducted at the port of final departure. Under special circumstances, it may be conducted at a place designated by the competent authority concerned.
No persons may embark or disembark, and no cargo or articles may be loaded or unloaded, on a means of transport exiting the country from the time after exit inspection until its exit, or on a means of transport entering the country from the time after entry until its entry inspection, without permission granted by the exit and entry border inspection authority in accordance with the prescribed procedures.

Article 51 The person in charge of a means of transport or the entity acting as an agent for the exit or entry business of means of transport shall, in accordance with the provisions, report to the exit and entry border inspection authority in advance the time of arrival and departure of the means of transport at the port and the place of stay, and truthfully declare information on crew members, passengers, cargo or articles.

Article 52 The person in charge of a means of transport or the entity acting as an agent for the exit or entry business of means of transport shall cooperate with the exit and entry border inspection, and shall immediately report and assist in the investigation and handling of any act found to be in violation of the provisions of this Law.
Where a means of transport entering the country carries persons who are not allowed to enter, the person in charge of the means of transport shall be responsible for taking them out of the country.

Article 53 The exit and entry border inspection authority shall, in accordance with the provisions, exercise supervision over means of transport exiting or entering the country under any of the following circumstances:
(1) A means of transport exiting the country during the period from the start of exit border inspection to the time of exit, or a means of transport entering the country during the period from entry to the completion of entry border inspection;
(2) A foreign vessel during its voyage on the inland waters of China; or
(3) Other circumstances where supervision is necessary.

Article 54 Persons who need to board or leave a foreign vessel for the purpose of loading or unloading articles, repair operations, visits, or other reasons shall apply to the exit and entry border inspection authority for a boarding permit.
Where the operation of laying alongside is needed between a Chinese vessel and a foreign vessel or between foreign vessels, the captain or the entity acting as an agent for the exit or entry business of means of transport shall apply to the exit and entry border inspection authority for completion of the vessel laying alongside formalities.

Article 55 Foreign vessels and aircraft shall navigate or fly along the prescribed routes or airways within the territory of China.
Vessels or aircraft exiting or entering the country shall not sail or fly into areas other than ports open to foreign countries. Where they sail or fly into such areas due to unforeseeable emergencies or force majeure, they shall immediately report to the nearest exit and entry border inspection authority or local public security organ, and shall be subject to supervision and administration.

Article 57 Entities engaged in agency business for the exit and entry of means of transportation shall file with the exit-entry border inspection authority. Personnel engaged in business agency shall have their employer go through the filing formalities with the exit-entry border inspection authority.

Article 58 The measures of on-the-spot interrogation, continued interrogation, detention for investigation, restriction on the scope of activities, and repatriation prescribed in this Chapter shall be implemented by the public security organ of the local people's government at or above the county level or the exit-entry border inspection authority.

Article 60 Where a foreigner falls under any of the circumstances prescribed in paragraph 1, Article 59 of this Law, and the suspicion cannot be eliminated through on-the-spot interrogation or continued interrogation, and further investigation is needed, the foreigner may be detained for investigation.
When imposing detention for investigation, a written decision on detention for investigation shall be presented, and interrogation shall be conducted within 24 hours. If it is found that detention for investigation shall not be imposed, the detention for investigation shall be immediately lifted.
The period of detention for investigation shall not exceed 30 days; where the case is complicated, upon approval by the public security organ of the local people's government at the next higher level or the exit-entry border inspection authority, the period may be extended to 60 days. For a foreigner whose nationality and identity are unknown, the period of detention for investigation shall be calculated from the date on which his/her nationality and identity are ascertained.
Article 63 Persons who are detained for investigation or who are decided to be repatriated but cannot be executed immediately shall be held in custody in detention houses or repatriation sites.

Article 64 Where a foreigner refuses to accept the measures of continued interrogation, detention for investigation, restriction on the scope of activities, or repatriation imposed on him/her according to the provisions of this Law, he/she may apply for administrative reconsideration according to law, and the decision on administrative reconsideration shall be final.
Where another overseas person refuses to accept the measure of repatriation imposed on him/her according to the provisions of this Law and applies for administrative reconsideration, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply.

Article 65 Where a decision is made according to law that a person is not allowed to exit or enter China, the deciding authority shall promptly notify the exit-entry border inspection authority; where the circumstances that cause the prohibition on exit or entry disappear, the deciding authority shall promptly revoke the decision prohibiting exit or entry and notify the exit-entry border inspection authority.

Article 66 Where necessary for maintaining national security and the order of exit/entry administration, the exit-entry border inspection authority may perform body checks on persons exiting or entering China. Body checks shall be conducted by two border inspection officers of the same gender as the person being checked.

Article 67 Where a visa, foreigner stay or residence permit, or other exit/entry document is damaged, lost, stolen, or robbed, or it is discovered after issuance that the holder does not meet the issuance conditions, the issuing authority shall declare the exit/entry document void.
Forged, altered, fraudulently obtained, or exit/entry documents declared void by the issuing authority are invalid.
The public security organ may cancel or confiscate the exit/entry documents prescribed in the preceding paragraph or those used by others under false pretenses.

Article 68 Means of transportation used for organizing, transporting, or assisting others in illegally exiting or entering China, and articles needed as evidence for case handling, may be seized by the public security organ.
Contraband items, documents and materials involving state secrets, and tools used for carrying out activities that violate exit/entry administration discovered and seized by the public security organ shall be seized and dealt with in accordance with relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 69 The authenticity of exit/entry documents shall be determined by the issuing authority, the exit-entry border inspection authority, or the exit/entry administration department of the public security organ.

Article 70 The administrative penalties prescribed in this Chapter, unless otherwise provided in this Chapter, shall be decided by the public security organ of the local people's government at or above the county level or the exit-entry border inspection authority; among them, a warning or a fine of not more than 5,000 yuan may be decided by the exit/entry administration department of the public security organ of the local people's government at or above the county level.

Article 72 Whoever assists others in illegally exiting or entering China shall be fined not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, shall be detained for not less than 10 days but not more than 15 days, and shall also be fined not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated.
Where a unit commits the act prescribed in the preceding paragraph, it shall be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan, and if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 73 Whoever obtains a visa, stay or residence permit, or other exit/entry document by fraud or false pretenses shall be fined not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 5,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, shall be detained for not less than 10 days but not more than 15 days, and shall also be fined not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan.
Where a unit commits the act prescribed in the preceding paragraph, it shall be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 74 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of this Law, issues an invitation letter or other application materials to a foreigner shall be fined not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated; and the person shall be ordered to bear the exit expenses of the invited foreigner.
Where a unit commits the act prescribed in the preceding paragraph, it shall be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated; and the unit shall be ordered to bear the exit expenses of the invited foreigner, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 75 Where a Chinese citizen who, after exiting China, illegally goes to another country or region and is repatriated, the exit-entry border inspection authority shall confiscate his/her exit/entry documents, and the exit/entry document issuing authority shall not issue exit/entry documents to him/her within six months to three years from the date of his/her repatriation.

Article 77 Where a foreigner, without approval, enters an area restricted to foreigners, he/she shall be ordered to leave immediately; if the circumstances are serious, he/she shall be detained for not less than five days but not more than ten days. Any written records, audio-visual materials, electronic data or other articles illegally obtained by the foreigner shall be confiscated or destroyed, and the tools used shall be confiscated.
Where a foreigner or a foreign institution, in violation of the provisions of this Law, refuses to comply with the decision made by a public security organ or a state security organ to move out within a specified time limit, a warning shall be given and a compulsory move-out shall be effected; if the circumstances are serious, the person directly responsible shall be detained for not less than five days but not more than fifteen days.

Article 78 Where a foreigner illegally resides, a warning shall be given; if the circumstances are serious, he/she shall be fined 500 yuan for each day of illegal residence, with a total amount not exceeding 10,000 yuan, or shall be detained for not less than five days but not more than fifteen days.
Where the guardian or other person with guardianship responsibility fails to fulfill guardianship obligations, causing a foreigner under the age of 16 to illegally reside, a warning shall be given to the guardian or other person with guardianship responsibility, and a fine of not more than 1,000 yuan may also be imposed.

Article 79 Where a person harbors or shelters foreigners who have illegally entered or illegally reside, assists such foreigners in evading inspection, or illegally provides exit/entry documents to foreigners who illegally reside, he/she shall be fined not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, he/she shall be detained for not less than five days but not more than fifteen days and shall also be fined not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan, and any illegal gains shall be confiscated.
Where a unit commits the act prescribed in the preceding paragraph, it shall be fined not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan, any illegal gains shall be confiscated, and the directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 80 Where a foreigner works illegally, he/she shall be fined not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, he/she shall be detained for not less than five days but not more than fifteen days and shall also be fined not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan.
Where a person acts as an agent for foreigners to work illegally, if the person is an individual, he/she shall be fined 5,000 yuan for each foreigner illegally introduced, with a total amount not exceeding 50,000 yuan; if the person is a unit, it shall be fined 5,000 yuan for each foreigner illegally introduced, with a total amount not exceeding 100,000 yuan; any illegal gains shall be confiscated.
Where a person illegally employs foreigners, he/she shall be fined 10,000 yuan for each foreigner illegally employed, with a total amount not exceeding 100,000 yuan; any illegal gains shall be confiscated.

Article 81 Where a foreigner engages in activities not corresponding to the purpose of stay or residence, or falls under other circumstances in which he/she violates Chinese laws or regulations and is no longer suitable to continue staying or residing in China, he/she may be ordered to leave China within a specified time limit.
Where a foreigner violates the provisions of this Law, if the circumstances are serious but the act does not constitute a crime, the Ministry of Public Security may impose expulsion. The penalty decision of the Ministry of Public Security shall be final.
A foreigner who has been expelled from China shall not be allowed to enter China within ten years from the date of expulsion.
Article 86 Where a fine of not more than 500 yuan is imposed for an act violating exit/entry administration, the exit/entry border inspection authority may make a penalty decision on the spot.

Article 87 Where a fine is imposed for an act violating exit/entry administration, the person subject to the penalty shall pay the fine at a designated bank within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the penalty decision. Where the person subject to the penalty has no fixed domicile at the locality, and it is difficult to enforce the fine afterwards if it is not collected on the spot, or if it is truly difficult for the person to pay the fine at a designated bank at the port, the fine may be collected on the spot.
Article 88 Where a violation of the provisions of this Law constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 89 For the purpose of this Law, the following terms shall have the meanings as defined below:
“Exit” means leaving the mainland of China for another country or region, leaving the mainland of China for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or the Macao Special Administrative Region, or leaving the mainland of China for the Taiwan region.
“Entry” means entering the mainland of China from another country or region, entering the mainland of China from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or the Macao Special Administrative Region, or entering the mainland of China from the Taiwan region.
“Foreigner” means a person who does not have Chinese nationality.

Article 90 With the approval of the State Council, provinces and autonomous regions bordering on neighboring countries may, in accordance with the boundary administration agreements concluded between China and the relevant countries, formulate local regulations or local government rules to regulate the movement of residents in the border areas between the two countries.

Article 91 Where other laws provide otherwise for the administration of the entry, exit, stay and residence of members of diplomatic missions or consular posts of foreign states in China and other foreigners who enjoy privileges and immunities, the provisions of those other laws shall prevail.

Article 92 A foreigner who applies for exit/entry documents such as visas, foreigner stay or residence permits, or applies for extension or alteration of such documents, shall pay the visa fees or certificate fees in accordance with the relevant provisions.

Article 93 This Law shall come into force as of July 1, 2013. The Law of the People's Republic of China on the Control of the Entry and Exit of Aliens and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Control of the Entry and Exit of Citizens shall be abolished simultaneously.
